info.name: Rolinse Stores API
info.description:
Rolinse Stores backend (Laravel + Sanctum bearer tokens) — see api_docs.md and architecture.md at the project root for the full reference this was built from.

## Before you run this

1. Start the API: `php artisan serve` (default `http://localhost:8000`).
2. Migrate + seed: `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed`. Seeders are idempotent (safe to re-run) as of this collection's date. Seeded accounts used below:
   - Admin (verified, role 1): `admin@example.com` / `12345678`
   - Regular user (verified, role 2): `user@example.com` / `12345678`
3. Import this collection plus `Rolinse - Local.postman_environment.json`, select the environment, then run **00 - Auth → Register** first (or **Login (Seeded User)** if you'd rather skip straight to an already-verified account).

## How auth works here

Bearer tokens (Sanctum personal access tokens), not cookies — much simpler than a cookie/CSRF-based SPA API. `Register` and `Login` both return a `token` field; a collection-level test script on every request automatically picks up `token` from the response body if present and stores it as `{{token}}`, and a pre-request script attaches `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` to every request automatically. You don't need to touch headers yourself anywhere in this collection.

## A registration quirk worth knowing

`POST /register` returns a token immediately and that token works for authenticated routes right away, but the account's `email_verified_at` is NOT set at registration — an OTP is generated (see `POST /verify-otp`) to verify it. Calling `POST /login` (as opposed to using the token you already have from registering) will fail with "Email not verified" until that OTP step completes, and the OTP is never returned in the API response (by design — it goes out via the notification channel). So: **use the token from Register directly** for the main customer journey below; `Login` is demonstrated separately against the pre-seeded, already-verified `user@example.com` account instead.

## Folder order

1. **00 - Auth** — register (primary path) + login (seeded account) + username/email/referral checks
2. **01 - Catalogue (Public)** — products, types, filter, category shop, best-sellers; harvests a product to buy
3. **02 - Deals (Public)**
4. **03 - My Account** — profile, shipping address, notifications, discount check, password change
5. **04 - Orders** — place an order (using the harvested product), order history
6. **05 - Payments (Reference)** — Stripe/Paystack/Flutterwave/PayPal initiate+verify; none of these can fully succeed without real gateway credentials in `.env` — see each request's description
7. **06 - Finance** — currency list
8. **07 - Admin - Auth** — logs in as the seeded admin, replacing the active session for every folder after this
9. **08 through 12 - Admin - \*** — products, orders (incl. status updates + sales analytics), customers, promo codes, delivery (Fez)
10. **13 - Delivery Webhook (Reference)** — not directly runnable (needs Fez's shared secret) — documents the contract

Run the whole collection top-to-bottom via Collection Runner for a coherent end-to-end story, or jump into any folder on its own once **00 - Auth** has set a token.

request.description: Price comes from the DB (product_id + quantity only) — the client can't influence the total by sending its own price. is_nigeria/is_benin are explicit here on purpose: omitting both used to silently route every order down the international-export path (fixed) — this shows the normal domestic case. weight/pickup_state are required (delivery_details.* — validated now; previously a missing one crashed with a raw 500 QueryException instead of a 422). Without real FEZ_* credentials in .env, the order still succeeds (201) but the response carries a `warning` that delivery scheduling failed — that's the expected fallback, not a bug.
Requires either an authenticated token (used here) or an explicit ?email= — a bare request with neither now returns a clean 422 instead of an empty 200.

item.name: 05 - Payments (Reference)
item.description: All four gateways verify server-to-server against the real provider (Paystack/Flutterwave/PayPal) or Stripe's SDK — none trust a client-supplied "success" claim, which is the important thing to know about this section. None of these will fully succeed without real gateway credentials in `.env`; they're included so the request shapes are documented, and each will fail cleanly (4xx/5xx from the provider call) rather than silently doing nothing.

item.name: 13 - Delivery Webhook (Reference)
item.description: Fez calls this directly (server-to-server), guarded by a shared secret rather than a login — set {{webhook_shared_secret}} to match WEBHOOK_SHARED_SECRET in .env to actually exercise it.

exec: pm.test('Correctly rejected: no shared secret configured', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

request.description: Without a matching secret this correctly 401s — that's the fix being demonstrated, not a bug. This route was previously open to the internet with a signature-check middleware that always returned true.
